sample_unit: nonpublic real-world admission records (retrospective phase); 28 physicians diagnosing 5 cases each (prospective phase)

links.outcome: Physician diagnostic accuracy with versus without LLM assistance, and effect of biased LLM outputs
links.effect: LLMs significantly improved diagnostic accuracy of less-experienced physicians; no significant benefit for specialists. When LLMs gave biased responses, physician performance often failed to improve or declined.
links.quote: In the prospective phase, LLMs significantly improved the diagnostic accuracy of less-experienced physicians; no significant benefit was observed for specialists.

links.outcome: Ranking stability of LLM diagnoses across repeated runs (Jaccard similarity, entropy)
links.effect: Higher accuracy often correlated with lower ranking stability across most LLMs.
links.quote: Interestingly, higher accuracy often correlated with lower ranking stability across most LLMs.

links.outcome: Physician performance when LLM outputs were biased or incorrect
links.effect: When LLMs generated biased responses, physician performance often failed to improve or even declined.
links.quote: However, when LLMs generated biased responses, physician performance often failed to improve or even declined.

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLMs on rare disease diagnostic cases and tests the impact of providing LLM diagnostic outputs to clinicians in a prospective study comparing physician accuracy across sequential access steps.
